headlines.title: Alphabet drops 12% in deepening tech and semiconductor rout
headlines.summary: A steep 12.6% sell-off in Alphabet (GOOGL) dragged down the broader market, pulling semiconductor and software names like Micron (MU), Intel (INTC), and Marvell (MRVL) deep into negative territory. Bucking the tech retreat, healthcare stocks offered a pocket of green as Eli Lilly (LLY), Merck (MRK), and Gilead (GILD) notched solid gains.

headlines.title: Learn Why The Bull Case For Micron Stock Could Change Following Memory Shortage Warning
headlines.summary: Micron Technology is in focus after SK Hynix reported record quarterly results and projected tight memory supply through 2030, while Micron continued to secure long term customer agreements and maintained its regular US$0.15 cash dividend that went ex dividend on 14 October 2026. The same supply constraints that SK Hynix links to AI and data center demand are feeding into Micron’s DRAM, HBM and NAND roadmap.

description: Micron Technology, Inc. engages in the provision of semiconductor memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Mainland China, other Asia Pacific countries, Japan, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Cloud Memory Business Unit, Core Data Center Business Unit, Mobile and Client Business Unit, and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit segments. The company provides dynamic random access memory (DRAM) products, including High-Bandwidth Memory, doublie data rate, low-power DRAM, and graphics DRAM products; NAND products comprising solid state drives, managed NAND, and multi-chip packages; and NOR products. The company sells its products under the Micron brand name and private labels through its own direct sales force, sales or representative offices, as well as through distributors, retailers, and independent sales representatives. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.
